The Schedule Intensity Index (I_s) quantifies how much a team’s performance may be compromised by the rigors of their game schedule. It is derived from the number and geographic spread of opponents, weighted by historical performance variance. Player Velocity Efficiency (E_v) captures the disproportionate impact of fast, agile players—especially those underweight—on game dynamics. Travel Degradation Factor (F_d) models the cumulative effect of long-distance travel on team readiness. These three operators form a triadic system where I_s and F_d act as external stressors, while E_v represents internal resilience. In GSE, these map to state transitions: high I_s and F_d reduce available tactical options, while high E_v increases dynamic flexibility. In GSI, they inform Bayesian priors on team outcomes, adjusting for schedule and travel effects. The failure mode occurs when all three factors align to produce a low-efficiency regime, indicating systemic vulnerability.
